title: Security Validation Runbook: Scope, Evidence Exports, and Remediations
content:
Purpose:
This runbook defines the operational approach for coordinating external security validations (third-party validation, red-team-style engagements, and compliance probes) focused on RBAC v2, audit log schema completeness, evidence automation, and SIEM export fidelity. It is intended for security engineers, SRE, platform owners, and the external assessment vendor liaison.

High-level objective:
- Provide a repeatable, low-friction engagement flow that delivers verifiable evidence artifacts suitable for SIEM ingestion and compliance audits.
- Reduce manual packaging time by automating collection of RBAC policy snapshots, audit streams, and archive-able evidence.
- Ensure remediation guidance is actionable and tied to observable signals in logs and dashboards.

Scope and exclusions:
- IN SCOPE: RBAC v2 policy definitions and scope (role, grant, deny rules), audit log schema for control plane and serving runtime (authentication, authorization, model-serving events), automated evidence exports for SIEM (Elastic, Splunk, Sumo Logic), packaging of artifacts for external teams.
- OUT OF SCOPE: Network perimeter scans, physical security reviews, customer data exfiltration analysis beyond synthetic test accounts. For data-sensitive investigations, use the private-deployments playbook.

Pre-engagement checklist (owner: security-engagement lead):
1) Confirm engagement statement of work and allowed test windows (linked as JIRA ticket).
2) Identify entry points and test accounts (service accounts, demo users). Ensure minimal production impact.
3) Create ephemeral log forwarding stream for the engagement to avoid mixing evidence (ev-ingest-<engagement-id>).
4) Lock down RBAC snapshot: run rbacsnap tool and store per the evidence manifest.
5) Notify SRE, platform, and on-call security engineers with pager schedule.

RBAC v2 checkpoints (what to capture):
- Full role definitions (including inherited roles and group memberships). Export in both YAML and flattened CSV for easy diffing.
- Effective permissions for designated test accounts (computed through role resolution).
- Privileged role membership changes during testing (time-series).
- Any temp elevation workflows (approval flows, just-in-time grants).
- Mapping of policy IDs to human-friendly names and owning team.

Audit log schema and required fields:
- Core fields to validate: timestamp, event_id, principal_id, principal_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, outcome (success|failure), request_id, correlation_id, raw_payload_ref.
- Serving-runtime extras: model_id, sequence_length, tokens_consumed, cached_prefix_hit (boolean), gpu_node_id.
- Control-plane extras: api_key_id, client_ip, region, route, rollout_tag.
- Recommended export format: NDJSON with one JSON event per line. Include a guaranteed ordering key (event_seq) to help reconstruct flows.

Evidence export formats and retention:
- Primary artifact set per engagement:
  - rbacsnap-<engagement>.yaml (complete role graph)
  - effective-perms-<engagement>.csv (flattened view)
  - audit-export-<engagement>.ndjson.gz (time-bounded, compressed)
  - export-manifest-<engagement>.json (index of artifacts with sha256 checksums)
  - siem-ingest-log-preview-<engagement>.txt (sanity spot-checks)
- Retention: store artifacts in secure object storage bucket with lifecycle: 90 days encrypted, 1 year archived (if requested by legal), deletion confirmation recorded.

Automated evidence collector (ev-collector) responsibilities:
- Triggered via a playbook run: collects RBAC snapshot, subscribes to a short-lived audit stream, performs live sampling for a configurable window (default 2 hours), and bundles artifacts.
- Supports adapters: S3 object export, GCS, and direct SIEM fastpath (HTTP collector endpoint).
- Produces an export-manifest with checksums and a human-friendly report: counts by action type, top principals, sample failures.

SIEM export and ingest pipeline (recommended):
1) Export NDJSON compressed artifacts from ev-collector to s3://security-evidence/<engagement>/audit-export.ndjson.gz.
2) Run siem-validate job: checks schema conformance (all required fields present), sample ingest to staging index (security-validation-<engagement>).
3) Provide vendor with read-only access to the staging index for the engagement window if needed.
4) After engagement, map fields to production SIEM pipeline (rename principal_id->user.id, correlation_id->trace.id, model_id->asset.id).

Remediation ladder and SLAs (for findings discovered during validation):
- P0 (critical, exploitation trivial): rollback or emergency fix within 4 hours, full post-fix evidence export, and a hotpatch PR assigned.
- P1 (high, privilege escalation possible): mitigation within 48 hours (policy revocation, temporary deny), full remediation plan in sprint backlog.
- P2 (medium, info disclosure or missing logs): resolution within 14 days with follow-up validation sampling.
- P3 (low, process/documentation): schedule for next quarter.

Tie findings to observable signals:
- Each finding must include: repro steps, evidence artifact references (manifest entries), affected RBAC IDs, and the audit log event IDs (event_id).
- Provide a query snippet for the SIEM to detect the condition (include sample KQL/DSL).

Communication and handoff:
- Outbound owner: security-engagement lead. Provide a one-page findings summary and attach export-manifest.
- Internal escalation: page platform-owner and SRE for P0/P1. Create a tracking JIRA and link evidence.
- Vendor handoff: grant ephemeral access credentials with an expiry to the relevant staging bucket and optional SIEM viewer.

Post-engagement verification and closure:
1) Confirm remediation artifacts and re-run ev-collector for the same test vectors.
2) Verify that SIEM detection queries now return expected remediation status (zero occurrences for the repro).
3) Produce a closure package: before/after RBAC snapshots, before/after digest of audit-export, and final remediation ticket links.

Operational examples (short):
- RBAC snapshot command: rbacsnap --output rbacsnap-eng-123.yaml --format yaml --include-system-roles
- Audit export window (2hr) with samplers: ev-collector run --start 2026-02-25T14:00Z --end 2026-02-25T16:00Z --out s3://security-evidence/eng-123/
- Sample SIEM detection (Elasticsearch painless-esque): query for events where action == "role/grant" and principal_type == "service_account" and outcome == "success" and timestamp >= start_window

Appendix A: Minimal export-manifest example (human-readable line):
- {artifact: rbacsnap-eng-123.yaml, sha256: <hex>, size_bytes: 234278, created: 2026-02-25T16:05:12Z}

Appendix B: Quick mapping guidance to RBAC v2 model names:
- policy_id -> policy.uuid
- role_name -> role.display_name
- member -> subject.id (type: user|group|service)

Open questions and follow-ups:
- Confirm whether external vendors require raw payloads (sensitive) or redacted payload_refs; default to redaction and provide raw on case-by-case approved request.
- Decide default evidence lifecycle policy for non-P0 engagements (90 days vs 180 days).
- Add a small service to automatically generate SIEM mapping recipes per engagement (epic: SEC-automation-2026).

Sign-off:
- Security-engagement lead (Aisha Kapoor) — draft in review with platform and SRE.
